title: How AI Chips Power the Intelligence Revolution

slides.heading: How AI Chips Power the Intelligence Revolution
slides.body: From GPUs to custom silicon — the hardware race driving modern AI

slides.heading: Why Regular CPUs Aren't Enough
slides.body: Traditional CPUs process tasks one at a time — great for general computing, but AI needs to perform millions of math operations simultaneously. Training a single large AI model can require more calculations than all of humanity has done in history.

slides.heading: The GPU: Accidentally Perfect for AI
slides.body: Graphics cards were designed to render pixels in parallel. Researchers discovered in the 2000s that GPUs were ideal for neural network math — matrix multiplications that run thousands of operations at once. NVIDIA's CUDA platform turned this insight into the backbone of modern AI.

slides.heading: Tensor Cores: Specialized AI Circuitry
slides.body: Modern AI chips include dedicated 'tensor cores' that accelerate the specific math AI uses — fused multiply-add operations on matrices. NVIDIA's H100 chip contains over 16,000 tensor cores, delivering hundreds of teraflops of AI performance on a single card.

slides.heading: Custom Silicon: Google's TPU
slides.body: Google built its own Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) in 2016 because off-the-shelf GPUs were too general-purpose. TPUs are custom-designed for exactly one job: running neural networks. They're more energy-efficient for inference and now power Google Search, Maps, and Gemini.

slides.heading: The Memory Bottleneck
slides.body: Chips need to move enormous amounts of data between processing cores and memory — a limit called 'memory bandwidth.' AI chips now use High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), stacked directly on the chip, delivering over a terabyte per second of data flow to keep thousands of cores fed.

slides.heading: Networking Thousands of Chips Together
slides.body: No single chip can train a frontier AI model. Data centers link thousands of GPUs with ultra-fast interconnects like NVLink and InfiniBand. Training GPT-4-scale models required over 25,000 NVIDIA A100s running in parallel for months — a supercomputer-scale operation.

slides.heading: Neuromorphic and Analog Chips
slides.body: The next frontier: chips that mimic the brain's own architecture. Intel's Loihi and IBM's NorthPole process information as spikes of activity — the same way neurons fire. These neuromorphic chips use a fraction of the energy of conventional AI hardware for certain tasks.

slides.heading: The Geopolitics of AI Chips
slides.body: AI chips are now a matter of national security. The most advanced chips require extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines made only by ASML in the Netherlands. Export controls on chips and chip-making equipment have become central to US-China geopolitical competition.

slides.heading: The Hardware Behind Every Breakthrough
slides.body: Every AI assistant, image generator, and language model runs on specialized silicon. The chip war is the intelligence war — whoever leads in AI hardware shapes the future of technology, economy, and global power.
